title: Reject a 1024-run ceiling for the measured terminal Uniform case
question: Can broad Linux descriptor headroom and existing memory admission remove substantial spill without slowing the 40 GiB complete job?
summary: One eligible fully verified pair regressed 14.61% elapsed with 43.85% fewer managed spill bytes. This exceeded the individual threshold for both rules. Stopped before the remaining timed pairs and removed the candidate.

workloads: 40 GiB Uniform followed by eight exact Balanced parts. 984 initial runs, m256, one worker, hard 1 GiB without swap.

validation.summary: Both selector-boundary suites, source pins, small output preflights, full paired warmup and one eligible complete pair passed independent scope checks.

limitations: One eligible pair and one synthetic WSL2/ext4 workload.
Managed byte volume and pushed kernel counters have separate scopes. Sampled descriptors are a lower bound on peak.
exclusions: Separate structural control, both warmups and two unattempted timing pairs.
reopen_when: Test a distinct schedule that bounds active readers independently of catalog size, or test admitted application-buffer sizing.
